theory.intro: A 3D problem is solved by finding the right-angled triangles hidden inside the solid or the scene. Solve the triangle that has enough information, then carry that result into the next one. Every angle made with a base sits inside one of these triangles.
facts: Find that base diagonal with Pythagoras first and keep it exact.
A **bearings** problem needs a top-down view: draw each direction from north, then add or subtract bearings to get the angle between them.
$\tan\theta=\dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}$, and $\tan^{-1}$, $\sin^{-1}$ or $\cos^{-1}$ of a ratio recovers the angle.
Keep every surd and calculator value **unrounded** until the last line, because rounding a diagonal early shifts the final angle.
steps: Break the solid or scene into right-angled triangles
Find any shared length, keeping surds exact
Use trigonometry to find the angle or distance

mastery.solution_text:
First find the perpendicular height $TC$, using the apothem $CM=\dfrac{12}{2}=6\text{ cm}$.
$TC^2=10^2-6^2$
$=64$
$TC=8\text{ cm}$
A slant edge reaches a corner, so its horizontal leg is half the base diagonal.
Base diagonal $=\sqrt{12^2+12^2}=12\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$, so $CQ=6\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$.
$\tan\theta=\dfrac{8}{6\sqrt{2}}$
$\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{8}{6\sqrt{2}}\right)$
$=43.31\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx43^{\circ}$

In the top-down right-angled triangle $PBQ$ (right angle at $B$), the $050^{\circ}$ bearing is the angle at $P$.
$PB=70\cos50^{\circ}$
$=44.99\ldots\text{ m}$
$BQ=70\sin50^{\circ}$
$=53.62\ldots\text{ m}$
Use the elevation from $P$ to find the tower height $h$.
$h=PB\times\tan33^{\circ}$
$=44.99\ldots\times\tan33^{\circ}$
$=29.22\ldots\text{ m}$
Now the elevation from $Q$.
$\tan\alpha=\dfrac{29.22\ldots}{53.62\ldots}$
$\alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{29.22\ldots}{53.62\ldots}\right)$
$=28.58\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx29^{\circ}$
